name.en-US: Sts. André de Soveral and Companions
name.pt-BR: Santos Mártires de Cunhaú e Uruaçu

prayerExcerpt.en-US: Praised be the Most Blessed Sacrament!

meta.face: André: an old priest of about seventy-three, clean-shaven, with a weathered, sun-browned, bony face, wide at the high cheekbones and narrowing to a long, square chin — a big, straight nose with a broad bridge, deep-set dark eyes under bushy white eyebrows and a firm, full-lipped mouth; a bald crown with a short fringe of white hair, the eyes lifted to the Host. Mateus: a sturdy man of about forty with weathered olive skin and a wide, short face with a broad, low forehead — a straight nose with a broad, rounded tip, round, wide-open dark eyes under thick, level black brows, heavy cheekbones, a rounded jaw and a wide, full mouth; short black hair, a neat black moustache and short chin beard, and a fervent upward gaze.
meta.basis: No portrait exists. André de Soveral was born c. 1572 and died at about seventy-three, killed at Cunhaú after the elevation at Mass; Mateus Moreira, a layman, is remembered for his last words. The faces are artistic choices from their ages and states of life.
meta.excerpt: Last words of St. Mateus Moreira at Uruaçu, 3 Oct 1645, as handed down by the Brazilian Church (Wikipédia, Santos Mártires de Cunhaú e Uruaçu; Consolata). Not from the formulary, whose collect is pt-BR only.
